cards.explanation: The word is Maker. The LORD calls Himself the One “…who formed you from the womb…” (Isaiah 44:2). Jacob is the name He uses here for His people. He also says He is the One “…who will help you…”, and I'd say that's a pretty good way to start a message, friends.

His first words are “Do not be afraid.” The LORD says, “Do not be afraid, O Jacob My servant…” (Isaiah 44:2). Just before this, He had spoken of destruction (Isaiah 43:28). Then He turns around and speaks to Jacob as His servant, the one He has chosen. I think that's a big breath of relief.

The answer is His Spirit. The LORD says, “I will pour out My Spirit on your descendants, and My blessing on your offspring.” (Isaiah 44:3). Water goes on the dry ground and the Spirit goes on the people. Dry ground doesn't have to do anything but sit there and get soaked, and I'd say that's a pretty easy job.

The answer is False. The text says the opposite of wilting. The LORD says, “They will sprout among the grass like willows by flowing streams.” (Isaiah 44:4). That's a picture of growing, with water close by. Water was just promised in the verse before, so the willows are set up well.

The answer is on his hand. The text says still another “…will write on his hand, ‘The LORD’s,’…” (Isaiah 44:5). A hand is right where he can see it all day. Three people, three ways of saying the same thing: they belong to the LORD. I'd have a tough time with this one, friends, since my mustache does all my handwork.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I am the first and I am the last, and there is no God but Me.” (Isaiah 44:6). Right after calling Himself the first and the last, He says there is no God but Him. No other god is named beside Him in that line.

The answer is that He told them long ago. He asks, “Have I not told you and declared it long ago?” (Isaiah 44:8). He's saying His people already heard it from Him. Anyone who wants to match Him has to foretell what's coming, and He says He already did. I'd like to see somebody try to top that, friends.

The answer is My witnesses. He tells them, “You are My witnesses!” (Isaiah 44:8). Right after saying “Do not tremble or fear,” He gives them a job. A witness is somebody who can say what they've seen and heard. I think that's a pretty big honor to be handed in the middle of a worry.
The answer is True. The LORD says, “There is no other Rock; I know not one.” (Isaiah 44:8). He doesn't just say there's no other. He adds that He knows not one.

The answer is that they fail to see or comprehend. The text says their witnesses “…fail to see or comprehend, so they are put to shame.” (Isaiah 44:9). Seeing and understanding are what's missing. Those are the two things the verse names.

The reason is that the craftsmen are only human. The text says, “…for the craftsmen themselves are only human.” (Isaiah 44:11). Human hands made the thing, and humans are the ones putting their trust in it. That's the reason the companions will be put to shame. It's a short reason, friends, and I think it hits hard.

The word is hungry. The text says, “Yet he grows hungry and loses his strength; he fails to drink water and grows faint.” (Isaiah 44:12). The man making the god is the one getting tired and worn out. He needs a snack break from his own project, friends. Meanwhile the thing he's building needs nothing.

The answer is a man. The text says he “…fashions it in the likeness of man, like man in all his glory, that it may dwell in a shrine.” (Isaiah 44:13). The idol is made to look like a person. So a man makes a thing shaped like a man and then looks to it for help. That's a circle if I ever saw one.

The answer is the rain. The text says, “He plants a laurel, and the rain makes it grow.” (Isaiah 44:14). The woodworker plants it, but the rain does the growing. Notice he can't take credit for that part. He gets the wood and the rain gets the work.

The answer is True. It's right there in the text: “He takes some of it to warm himself, and he kindles a fire and bakes his bread.” (Isaiah 44:15). The same wood that keeps him warm and bakes his bread is the wood he's about to make into a god. I'd be nervous about that, friends.

The word is god. The text says, “He also fashions it into a god and worships it; he makes an idol and bows down to it.” (Isaiah 44:15). The same wood that fed his fire becomes the thing he bows to. A tree went from fuel to a thing he worships. I think that should make a person stop and scratch his head.

He asks it to save him. He bows down and prays, “Save me, for you are my god.” (Isaiah 44:17). He's asking to be saved by something made from the leftover wood. The verse before has him warm from the fire on the other half. I think that tells you which half did the useful work.

The reason is that their eyes and minds have been shut. The text says, “…He has shut their eyes so they cannot see and closed their minds so they cannot understand.” (Isaiah 44:18). That's the reason this verse gives for why they don't see how foolish it is. It's a hard verse, friends, and I think it's worth sitting with.

The word is ashes. The text says, “He feeds on ashes.” (Isaiah 44:20). Earlier, he burned half of the wood to roast meat and eat (Isaiah 44:16). This verse then says he feeds on ashes, and ashes won't fill anybody, friends.

The answer is False. He can't see it. The text says he “…cannot deliver himself…” (Isaiah 44:20). The thing is right there in his right hand, and he still can't ask whether it's a lie. His deluded heart has led him astray.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a mist.” (Isaiah 44:22). Clouds and mist are the kind of thing that clears away. I think that's one of the loveliest lines in the whole passage. It's a gift for Jacob, whom the LORD has called His servant.

The word is return. The LORD says, “Return to Me, for I have redeemed you.” (Isaiah 44:22). The reason is already in the sentence: He has redeemed them. So the door is open before they even take a step. I think anyone would want to come back to that.

The reason is that the LORD has redeemed Jacob. The text says, “For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and revealed His glory in Israel.” (Isaiah 44:23). That's the reason for the song. The heavens are told to sing for joy, the depths of the earth to shout aloud, and the mountains, forests and trees to break forth in song. That's a lot of voices, friends, and I think it's worth listening.
